title: Defining HR Critical Success Factors
desc: A one-page guide to defining HR critical success factors: eight steps from business strategy to stakeholder validation, how a CSF differs from a KPI and a target, and a worked example for the talent and leadership pipeline.

title: From Sacred Text to Statute: Human Resource Management Principles Across Religious Traditions, Cultural Norms, and the Code of Hammurabi
venue: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews, 31(03), pp. 1430–1436
desc: Compares people-management principles in the Code of Hammurabi and in Jewish, Christian, Islamic, Buddhist, Indic and Chinese traditions across seven dimensions, and finds a shared ethical core.

title: The Job Effectiveness Description: A Conceptual Framework Integrating Key Behavioral, Operational, and Performance Indicators into the Traditional Job Description
venue: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews, 31(03), pp. 953–958
desc: Proposes a job description that carries three kinds of indicators in one document: how the person acts, how the work runs, and what results it produces.

short: HR in the Post-Crisis Middle East
title: Critical Roles of Human Resource Management in Transforming and Adapting Organizations in the Post-Crisis Middle East
venue: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews, 31(02), pp. 1167–1176
desc: Sets out seventeen roles HR must play when organizations are rebuilt after conflict and disruption, and proposes the HR RESET framework, drawing on Syria, Lebanon, Iraq and the Gulf states.

short: AI and Culture in the Gulf
title: The Future Impact of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation on Organizational Culture
venue: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews, 31(02), pp. 985–995
desc: How AI and digital transformation reshape organizational culture, with evidence from Saudi Arabia, the UAE and the wider Gulf. Argues that cultural change is a prerequisite of successful AI adoption, not a by-product.

title: The 7 Gates of HRM: A Strategic Framework for Transforming People Management
desc: A framework that treats HR as a journey through seven gates: strategy, talent, learning, performance, rewards, culture and digital intelligence. Each gate prepares the organization for the next.

short: The Godfather Handbook for HR Executives
title: The Godfather Handbook for Human Resources Executives
desc: Inspired by the Godfather trilogy, a guide to power, loyalty, influence and judgment for the HR executive who intends to shape the organization rather than serve it. Foundations, six pillars, five cases and a closing code.

title: Nights with Ancestors: A Journey into the Past
desc: A journey into the past that asks what great figures would say about management and leadership today, with a chapter each on Drucker, Socrates, Marcus Aurelius, Maslow, Alexander the Great, Mary P. Follett, Salahuddin Ayyubi, Attila the Hun and Augustus.

short: The Divine Comedy in People Management
title: The Divine Comedy in People Management
desc: Reads people management through Dante Alighieri's Divine Comedy, for leaders who want to guide people, elevate purpose and pursue excellence.

short: Measuring What Matters Most for HR
title: Measuring What Matters Most for Human Resources: Key Performance Indicators and Key Operational Indicators
desc: A practical guide to measuring HR with key performance and key operational indicators, from building a data-driven HR culture to talent acquisition, engagement, retention, learning and performance management.

short: The Art of War for HR
title: The Art of War: Concise Human Resources Applications
desc: Reads Sun Tzu's Art of War as a handbook for people management and turns it into ten principles, from staffing, culture and reward to change, appraisal and strategy, with takeaways for practitioners.

short: The Black Holes of HR Management
title: The Black Holes of Human Resources Management
desc: A frank look at why HR fails and where it quietly loses value: eleven “black holes” from recruitment and appraisal to measurement and succession planning, plus the case for earning a seat at the table.

short: Give Your HR Function a Facelift
title: Give Your HR Function a Facelift
desc: The face of HR is changing in the era of the Fourth Industrial Revolution. Looks at why HR management has failed, where corruption creeps in, the forces reshaping work, and how AI and data will change the function.

short: Can HR Prevent the Great Extinction?
title: Can and Will HR Prevent the Great Extinction?
desc: Considers the impact of AI on HR practices: where it will first change recruitment and training, the concerns that slow its adoption, and a call for HR to respond to change rather than be replaced by it.

title: Reengineer Your Job Descriptions?
desc: Argues that traditional job descriptions rarely deliver the results organizations want, and proposes adding key performance indicators and critical success factors, a step toward the Job Effectiveness Description.

title: HRM Governance Is a Must!
desc: Why HR practices need governance: the conflict of interest in HR’s many roles, the dilemma of right versus right, and the corruption risks in recruitment, training, appraisal and pay, with a road map of governing bodies and tools.

title: When HR Meets Marketing
desc: Draws a parallel between marketing and HR, with a side-by-side table of eight shared themes, from portfolio and communication to loyalty, brand and satisfaction, and argues that HR can learn from marketing, especially on employer branding.

short: Become a More Effective HR Executive
title: Become a More Effective HR Executive
desc: Draws on Peter Drucker’s insights to help HR practitioners grow: five habits to master, from managing time to making decisions, and a fourteen-step plan from the author’s own experience as a CHRO during the 2008–2009 crisis.

short: What Does HR Do and Deliver?
title: What Does HR Do and What Does It Deliver?
desc: HR must measure what matters. Proposes five levels of HR measurement: strategic contribution, value added, people management, HR impact and HR effectiveness, and how to choose a framework that fits the organization.

title: Why Corporate Training Efforts Fail
desc: Why companies spend millions on training and still see little change: weak needs analysis, shallow evaluation and the difficulty of measuring return on investment. Describes five types of evaluation and how to approach ROI.

title: Profession in Transition
desc: The HR function is moving part of its work into the hands of line managers. Explains why HR is shifting from personnel administration to strategy, what that asks of line managers, and how the two should work together.

title: Learn from Ancient Times to Present Moments
desc: Looks at the leadership of Attila the Hun through the four main HR operations: staffing, performance management, rewards, and training and development, and asks what history can still teach HR.

short: HR Lessons from Sun Tzu, Part Two
title: HR Lessons from Sun Tzu’s The Art of War, Part Two
desc: Part two of the series applies Sun Tzu’s principles to HR: staffing, culture, rewards and training, each tied to practical HR work such as selection, organizational culture and pay for performance.

title: Learn Lessons from War for Prosperity in Peace Time
desc: A conversation on why HR professionals can learn from Sun Tzu’s Art of War: how military history informs business, where competition resembles warfare, and why managing people is a matter of life and death for an organization.

title: HR Ethics Revisited
desc: Examines the ethical side of HR practice, from appraisal and training to pay, recruitment and termination, and argues that HR needs the courage to question unethical practices before they damage the organization.

title: Attract and Retain Employees
desc: Argues that the shortage of talent is partly a myth and that employers suffer from “functional blindness”. Explores five delusions about hiring and retention and makes the case to stop recruiting and start attracting, through culture, brand and development.

title: Prevent Performance Crunch
desc: Why performance appraisal still frustrates managers and employees, and two problems behind it: a communication dilemma and the conflicting roles managers are asked to play. Offers practical steps to separate feedback from pay decisions and to help managers hold honest conversations.

title: “Overqualified” Is a Nonsense Term
desc: Argues that rejecting strong candidates as “overqualified” is a costly myth, and that the shortage of talent is often a failure of the employer’s own thinking. Makes the case for hiring the best and training where gaps remain.

title: Prevent Training Myopia in Your Company
desc: Why organizations cut training first when times are hard, and how to treat it as a strategic tool instead. Describes the proactive, active and reactive views of the training function.

short: HR Strategist or Tactician, Part Two
title: HR Strategist or Tactician? Part Two
desc: What being strategic really means, with a story of opening luxury villas without staff and a plan that cut expatriates by a quarter, and three places to start: productivity, competitive advantage and employer brand.

short: HR Strategist or Tactician, Part One
title: HR Strategist or Tactician? Part One
desc: Separates being strategic from being a strategic partner, through stories of HR managers who claimed a strategic role they could not explain, and describes the transactional, tactical and strategic hats HR wears.

short: Do You Feel Like Mr/Mrs Excluded?
title: Do You Feel Like Mr/Mrs Excluded?
desc: Three situations in which HR is left out of the decisions that matter, from opening a new branch to setting annual goals, and a call for top management to see the function from the inside.

short: Managing HR in Trying Times, Part Two
title: Managing HR in Trying Times, Part Two
desc: Practical guidance on downsizing: preparing people, protecting morale, leaving with respect, and a thirteen-step plan from the author’s own experience as a group CHRO in late 2008.

short: Managing HR in Trying Times, Part One
title: Managing HR in Trying Times, Part One
desc: How HR can step up when business is under pressure: the roles and rules of a downturn, keeping people committed, and why trying times are not only economic.

title: When It Comes to Retention, It’s Keep or Weep
desc: A guide to retention strategy: what really drives people to leave, the indicators that predict turnover, and six areas of focus, from competitive advantage to organizational development.

title: Naked Truth About HR Revealed, Part Two: Recipe for Failure
desc: Why HR practitioners so often stay inside the box, why top management shares the blame, and the questions every CEO should answer before judging the function. With stories from Egypt and Syria.

title: Naked Truth About HR Revealed, Part One: Do We Really Hate HR?
desc: A candid look at why HR is often not taken seriously, told through five snapshots from the author's career.
